evals.prompt: I want to learn TypeScript properly, I know JS well already. Use the official TS handbook (https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/intro.html) as material. I've got about 2 weeks, 3hrs/day. Build me a pool.
evals.expected_output: A learning-pool directory with an overview file (topic, concept list, calibration notes, chosen exercise-authorship mode, arc summary) and per-day files sized to ~14 days at 3hrs/day, starting from an intermediate/JS-fluent baseline rather than absolute basics, referencing or grounded in the official TS handbook, with self-checks per day and at least one weekly exam checkpoint. No project brief or grading content.
expectations: An overview file exists that names the topic, a concept list, calibration notes, and the chosen exercise-authorship mode (pointer or grounded)
Day-by-day files exist, sized to roughly 2 weeks (around 10-14 day files) rather than a fixed generic length
Day content is grounded in or explicitly points to the official TypeScript handbook rather than generic TS knowledge disconnected from any material
The starting difficulty assumes JS fluency (e.g. skips 'what is a variable'-level content) rather than starting from absolute zero
Each day file includes a distinct self-check section separate from the main task(s)
At least one weekly or final exam/checkpoint file exists, separate from the daily files
No day or exam file contains a worked solution/answer to its own exercise
No full multi-day capstone project brief is included; scope stays within roadmap, daily exercises, and exams

Each day file includes a distinct self-check section separate from the main task(s)

No full multi-day capstone project brief is included; scope stays within roadmap, daily exercises, and exams
